samples.question: The cream board carries small decorative coloured squares lying on the bare board; none of them touches a grid and none of them means anything. There are exactly six GRIDS on the board. Every grid is a 4-by-4 arrangement of sixteen square cells inside a solid frame, and each cell is either black (filled) or cream (empty). Two of the grids are STENCILS: a stencil is the grid whose frame is dark slate, and the two stencils sit at two opposite corners of the board. The KEY pattern is the cell-by-cell OVERLAY of the two stencils: a cell of the key is filled when that same cell is filled in either stencil or in both, and empty only when that cell is empty in both stencils. Neither stencil on its own gives the key. The other four grids are TILES: a tile is a grid whose frame is red, blue, green or purple, and the four tiles carry those four different frame colours. Exactly one tile's sixteen cells match the key pattern exactly, cell for cell; each of the other three tiles differs from the key in at least one cell. Grid positions, which corner holds which stencil, how many cells are filled, and the board clutter carry no other information. What is the frame colour of the tile whose pattern matches the key exactly? Answer red, blue, green or purple.
